lead: Recent developments highlight the intersection of climate change with technology, fisheries, and historical exploration.

stories.title: The real mystery behind Moana: After 1,700 years, why did Polynesians suddenly sail east?
stories.summary: New research sheds light on the reasons behind the Polynesian voyages to the east after a long period of stagnation. The study suggests that climate changes may have played a crucial role in motivating these long-distance sea travels. This historical context enriches our understanding of how ancient cultures adapted to environmental shifts.

stories.title: Datacentres drive up big tech’s carbon emissions to a third of those of France
stories.summary: A report reveals that the carbon emissions from major tech companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google have surged, now accounting for nearly a third of France's total emissions. This increase is primarily attributed to the rapid construction of datacentres. Despite this rise, the companies maintain their commitment to achieving net-zero emissions.

stories.title: El Niño Is Already Wreaking Havoc on Pacific Fisheries
stories.summary: The current El Niño phenomenon is causing significant disruptions in Pacific fisheries, with some areas facing severe challenges while others benefit from the warm waters. This situation highlights the complex impacts of climate change on marine ecosystems and the fishing industry. Stakeholders are urged to adapt to these shifting conditions to sustain their livelihoods.

stories.title: Datacentres drive up big tech’s carbon emissions to a third of those of France
stories.summary: The environmental impact of large tech firms is under scrutiny as their datacentres contribute significantly to global carbon emissions. In the last fiscal year, emissions rose sharply, prompting calls for more sustainable practices. The companies are facing pressure to balance growth with their sustainability goals.

stories.title: Meet the 8 South Australian space startups accelerating to the stars
stories.summary: A new wave of South Australian startups is emerging, focusing on innovative solutions that address climate risks through technology. These companies are exploring various applications, from AI-driven climate analysis to sustainable practices in space missions. Their work represents a forward-thinking approach to tackling environmental challenges.
